name: Imperial Blue
lede: Imperial Blue is a deep blue with a grand name, part of a small family of colors that borrowed "imperial" from the yellow of the Chinese court.

sections.title: The name
sections.body: Paterson defines imperial blue as a deep blue, and as a dye [1]. His entry for the prefix says "imperial" was first used for imperial yellow and then borrowed by other colours with pretensions of majesty [2].

sections.title: The imperial family
sections.body: Imperial yellow was a deep yellow that originated in yellow porcelain from China, a color reserved for the imperial court [2]. Imperial red is a deep bluish red, and imperial green is another name for emerald green [2]. Paterson gives the blue no court history of its own [2].

sections.title: Neighbors
sections.body: Close relatives in our list are [[royal-blue]], [[mazarine-blue]] and [[midnight-blue]], plus [[imperial-red]] and [[emerald-green]] from the same naming habit [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #353D82 measures lightness 28.7, chroma 44.2 and hue angle 295 degrees, a dark, saturated blue leaning slightly toward violet [3].
